title: MONGODB brocode
content:
MongoDB Complete Notes (From "MongoDB in One Hour" Video)

1. What is MongoDB?

  • MongoDB is a NoSQL database management system.
  • It can handle a huge amount of data and is used by many big tech companies.
  • NoSQL = "Not Only SQL" — data is stored in formats other than traditional SQL tables.
  • In SQL, data is stored in rows and columns (tables).
  • In MongoDB, related data is stored together as a single document (like one row in SQL).
  • Data inside a document is stored as field-value pairs, similar to JSON — but technically it's BSON (Binary JSON). It behaves the same way for practical use.
  • Main idea: data that is used together is stored together, instead of splitting it across separate tables (avoids painful SQL joins).

Structure of MongoDB

  • Document → group of field-value pairs (represents one object/record).
  • Collection → group of one or more documents. (TABLE)
  • Database → group of one or more collections. 
  • This structure makes scaling and working with data very easy.

Prerequisites

  • Basic knowledge of any object-oriented programming language (Python, Java, C++, C#, JavaScript — any one is fine).

2. Installing MongoDB

  1. Go to mongodb.com → Resources → Server → Installation.
  2. Choose your OS (Windows/Mac/Linux) and follow numbered steps for MongoDB Community Edition.
  3. Go to Download Center → select version & platform → download installer.
  4. Run installer:
    • Accept license agreement.
    • Choose "Complete" install.
    • Make sure "Install MongoDB as a Service" is checked.
    • Also install MongoDB Compass (GUI tool).
  5. Compass = graphical interface to manage your database. Click green Connect button to connect.

Installing MongoDB Shell (mongosh)

  1. Go to Download Center → MongoDB Shell → select version/platform → download.
  2. Unzip the folder → go to bin folder → copy the file path of the executable.
  3. Add this path to Environment Variables (System Properties → Advanced → Environment Variables → New variable, e.g., name it sh, paste the path).
  4. Now you can open the shell from anywhere by typing sh.
    • sh → connect to database
    • cls → clear screen
    • exit → exit the shell

Using VS Code for MongoDB

  1. Install the MongoDB extension in VS Code.
  2. Click the MongoDB icon → click localhost to connect.
  3. Right-click → Launch MongoDB Shell to open the terminal inside VS Code.
  4. Same commands apply: exit, sh, cls.

3. Creating and Using Databases

Command What it does
show dbs Shows all existing databases
use <dbname> Switches to a database (creates it if it doesn't exist)
db.createCollection("name") Creates a new collection
db.dropDatabase() Deletes the current database

Important note: A newly created database won't show up in show dbs until it has at least one collection with data — empty databases are invisible.

In Compass (GUI way)

  • Click green button to create database → give database name + first collection name → Create.
  • To delete: select database from sidebar → click trash icon → type name to confirm → Drop Database.

4. Inserting Documents

In Shell

  • Insert one document:
    db.students.insertOne({ name: "SpongeBob", age: 30, gpa: 3.2 })
  • View documents: db.students.find()
  • Insert many documents at once using insertMany() with an array of documents: 
    db.students.insertMany([  { name: "Patrick", age: 38, gpa: 1.5 },  { name: "Sandy", age: 27, gpa: 4.0 },  { name: "Gary", age: 18, gpa: 2.5 }])
  • Documents don't need to have the same fields — MongoDB is flexible like that.

In Compass

  • Go to collection → Add Data → Insert Document (or import JSON/CSV).
  • Type field-value pairs manually, or paste an array for multiple documents.
  • Use the Format button to fix formatting warnings, then click Insert.

5. Basic Data Types in MongoDB

Data Type Meaning Example
String Series of text in quotes name: "Larry"
Integer Whole number, no decimals age: 32
Double Number with decimal gpa: 2.8
Boolean true or false only fullTime: false
Date Date/time object using new Date() registerDate: new Date()
new date idle way me user show krta h 
Null No value / placeholder graduationDate: null
Array Field with multiple values in [ ] courses: ["Biology", "Chemistry", "Calculus"]
Nested Document A document inside a document address: { street: "123 Fake Street", city: "Bikini Bottom", zip: "12345" }
  • new Date() with no arguments = current date/time in UTC.
  • Nested documents are great for things like addresses.

6. Sorting and Limiting Documents

Sort

db.students.find().sort({ name: 1 })   // 1 = ascending (A-Z)
db.students.find().sort({ name: -1 })  // -1 = descending (Z-A)
  • Same logic works for numbers like GPA (1 = low to high, -1 = high to low).

Limit

db.students.find().limit(1)   // returns only 1 document
db.students.find().limit(3)   // returns only 3 documents

Combine sort + limit

db.students.find().sort({ gpa: -1 }).limit(1)   // student with highest GPA
db.students.find().sort({ gpa: 1 }).limit(1)    // student with lowest GPA

In Compass

  • Click "More Options" → add sort criteria (e.g., { name: 1 }) → Find.
  • Use the Limit box to restrict number of results (or leave blank/0 to return all).

7. The find() Method

  • db.students.find() → returns all documents.
  • find() takes two optional parameters:
    1. Query parameter — selection filter (like SQL's WHERE clause).
    2. Projection parameter — which fields to show/hide.
    3. .find({query},{projection})

Query examples

db.students.find({ name: "SpongeBob" })
db.students.find({ gpa: 4.0 })
db.students.find({ fullTime: false })
  • Multiple filters can be comma-separated (acts like AND).

Projection examples

db.students.find({}, { name: true, gpa: true, _id: false })
  • Set field to true (or 1) to include it, false (or 0) to exclude it.
  • _id is always returned by default unless you set it to false.

In Compass

  • Type filter in the Find text box, e.g. { name: "SpongeBob" }.
  • Use More Options → Project to choose which fields to show.

8. Updating Documents

updateOne() — updates a single document

db.students.updateOne(
  { name: "SpongeBob" },              // filter: which document to find
  { $set: { fullTime: true } }        // update: what to change
)
  • $set operator → adds a new field or changes an existing field's value.
  • It's safer to filter by _id since names can repeat and _id is always unique:
db.students.updateOne({ _id: ObjectId("...") }, { $set: { fullTime: false } })

Removing a field — $unset

db.students.updateOne({ _id: ObjectId("...") }, { $unset: { fullTime: "" } })
  • Set the field to an empty string "" inside $unset to remove it.

updateMany() — updates multiple documents at once

db.students.updateMany({}, { $set: { fullTime: false } })   // empty {} = select ALL documents

Checking if a field exists — $exists

db.students.updateMany(
  { fullTime: { $exists: false } },   // find docs missing this field
  { $set: { fullTime: true } }
)

In Compass

  • Click the pencil icon to edit a document.
  • Click trash icon next to a field to remove it.
  • Click plus (+) icon to add a new field, choose its data type, then click Update.

9. Deleting Documents

  • Before deleting, it's a good idea to export your collection (Compass → Export → choose JSON or CSV) so you can re-import later if needed.

deleteOne() — deletes a single matching document

db.students.deleteOne({ name: "Larry" })

deleteMany() — deletes multiple documents

db.students.deleteMany({ fullTime: false })

Delete documents missing a field

db.students.deleteMany({ registerDate: { $exists: false } })

In Compass

  • Click the trash can icon next to a document to delete it directly.
  • To bring data back: Add Data → Import JSON/CSV file (using your earlier export).

10. Comparison Operators

All comparison operators start with a $ sign.

Operator Meaning Example
$ne Not equal { name: { $ne: "SpongeBob" } }
$lt Less than { age: { $lt: 20 } }
$lte Less than or equal to { age: { $lte: 27 } }
$gt Greater than { age: { $gt: 27 } }
$gte Greater than or equal to { age: { $gte: 27 } }
$in Matches any value in a given array { name: { $in: ["SpongeBob","Patrick","Sandy"] } }
$nin Does NOT match any value in array { name: { $nin: ["SpongeBob","Patrick","Sandy"] } }

Range example (combine two operators on same field)

db.students.find({ gpa: { $gte: 3, $lte: 4 } })   // GPA between 3 and 4

11. Logical Operators

All logical operators return results based on true/false expressions.

Operator Meaning
$and ALL conditions must be true
$or AT LEAST ONE condition must be true
$nor ALL conditions must be false
$not Reverses/negates a condition

$and example

db.students.find({
  $and: [ { fullTime: true }, { age: { $lte: 22 } } ]
})

$or example

db.students.find({
  $or: [ { fullTime: true }, { age: { $lte: 22 } } ]
})

$nor example

db.students.find({
  $nor: [ { fullTime: true }, { age: { $lte: 22 } } ]
})

$not example — special benefit: includes null values too

db.students.find({ age: { $not: { $gte: 30 } } })
  • Normal $lt: 30 would skip documents where age is null.
  • $not will correctly include those null age documents too — useful when data is incomplete.

12. Indexes

  • An index allows faster lookup of a field.
  • Trade-off: indexes use more memory and make insert/update/delete operations slower.
  • MongoDB stores indexes as a B-tree data structure.
  • Best used on fields you search often but don't update often.

Checking performance without index

db.students.find({ name: "Larry" }).explain("executionStats")
  • Without an index, MongoDB does a linear search (checks every document one by one) — slow for large datasets.

Creating an index

db.students.createIndex({ name: 1 })   // 1 = ascending, -1 = descending
  • After creating the index, the same query examines far fewer documents (faster).

Managing indexes

db.students.getIndexes()          // lists all indexes
db.students.dropIndex("name_1")   // removes an index by name
  • Note: MongoDB automatically creates an index on _id by default.

In Compass

  • Go to the Indexes tab → Create Index → choose field & order (ascending/descending).
  • To delete: click trash icon → type index name to confirm.

13. Working with Collections

show collections                          // lists all collections in current database
db.createCollection("teachers")           // create a simple collection
db.courses.drop()                         // delete a collection

Advanced collection options

db.createCollection("teachers", {
  capped: true,        // limits collection size
  size: 10000000,      // max size in bytes (here: 10 MB)
  max: 100,            // max number of documents allowed
  autoIndexId: false   // whether to auto-create an index on _id (true/false)
})
  • capped: true requires you to also set a size.
  • max limits the total number of documents allowed in that collection.
  • autoIndexId controls whether an index is automatically applied to _id.
    • Indexes = faster reads, but slower writes — so there's a trade-off either way.

Quick Summary Cheat-Sheet

Task Shell Command
Show databases show dbs
Switch/create database use dbname
Show collections show collections
Create collection db.createCollection("name")
Insert one db.col.insertOne({...})
Insert many db.col.insertMany([{...},{...}])
Find all db.col.find()
Find with filter db.col.find({field: value})
Sort db.col.find().sort({field: 1/-1})
Limit db.col.find().limit(n)
Update one db.col.updateOne(filter, {$set:{...}})
Update many db.col.updateMany(filter, {$set:{...}})
Remove a field {$unset:{field: ""}}
Delete one db.col.deleteOne(filter)
Delete many db.col.deleteMany(filter)
Create index db.col.createIndex({field: 1})
Get indexes db.col.getIndexes()
Drop index db.col.dropIndex("indexname")
Drop collection db.col.drop()
Drop database db.dropDatabase()
